questions.stem: The 'MASTER GLAND' of the human endocrine system is the:

options.option_text: Thyroid gland in the neck region
Pituitary gland at the base of the brain
Pancreas behind the lower stomach area
Thymus in the upper chest cavity

questions.explanation: PITUITARY (hypophysis) — pea-sized gland at the base of the brain, sits in the sella turcica. Called 'master gland' because it controls many other endocrine glands via tropic hormones — TSH (→ thyroid), ACTH (→ adrenal cortex), FSH/LH (→ gonads), GH (growth), prolactin (milk), ADH/oxytocin (posterior). Itself controlled by the hypothalamus. Distractor 1 = thyroid. Distractor 3 = pancreas. Distractor 4 = thymus (immune development).

questions.stem: INSULIN, which lowers blood glucose, is secreted by which cells?

options.option_text: Alpha cells in the islets of Langerhans
Beta cells in the islets of Langerhans
Acinar cells of the exocrine pancreas
Adrenal cortex cells of the kidney top

questions.explanation: Pancreatic islets of Langerhans contain: ALPHA cells (~20%) — secrete GLUCAGON (raises glucose); BETA cells (~70%) — secrete INSULIN (lowers glucose); DELTA cells (~5%) — secrete somatostatin. Type 1 diabetes — autoimmune destruction of beta cells. Distractor 3 = exocrine pancreas (digestive enzymes). Distractor 4 = adrenal cortex (cortisol, aldosterone).

questions.stem: ADRENALINE (epinephrine) — the 'fight or flight' hormone — is secreted by the:

options.option_text: Adrenal cortex of the gland's outer layer
Adrenal medulla, the inner core of the gland
Pancreas in islets of Langerhans cells
Pituitary in its anterior front lobe

questions.explanation: Adrenal gland sits atop each kidney. Two parts: CORTEX (outer) — secretes steroid hormones (cortisol — stress; aldosterone — Na/K balance; androgens — sex hormones in small amounts). MEDULLA (inner) — secretes ADRENALINE (epinephrine) + NORADRENALINE during stress: heart rate ↑, blood pressure ↑, glucose ↑, pupils dilate, airways open. Sympathetic nervous system extension. Distractors 3, 4 are different glands.

questions.stem: The hormone responsible for the development of MALE secondary sexual characteristics is:

options.option_text: Oestrogen, also called the female hormone
Testosterone, secreted mainly by the testes
Progesterone, related to pregnancy support
Insulin, controls blood glucose levels

questions.explanation: TESTOSTERONE — secreted by Leydig cells in testes (small amount in adrenal cortex + ovaries too). Drives male puberty: deepening voice, facial + body hair, muscle development, sperm production. Stimulated by LH from anterior pituitary. Females also have low testosterone (libido, bone density). Distractor 1 = oestrogen (female puberty: breast development, menstruation, body fat distribution). Distractor 3 = progesterone (uterine lining, pregnancy maintenance). Distractor 4 = insulin (glucose).

questions.stem: Excess production of GROWTH HORMONE (GH) in adults causes:

options.option_text: Cretinism, with stunted growth and intellectual delay
Acromegaly, enlargement of hands, feet, jaw, and brow
Diabetes insipidus, with very dilute urine output
Goitre, with enlargement of the thyroid gland alone

questions.explanation: GH excess in ADULTS (after growth plates close) → ACROMEGALY: thickened bones in hands/feet/face, coarsened features. Often caused by a pituitary tumour. GH excess in CHILDREN (before plates close) → GIGANTISM (very tall stature). GH deficiency in children → dwarfism. Distractor 1 = cretinism (childhood hypothyroidism). Distractor 3 = ADH deficiency. Distractor 4 = thyroid disorder (often iodine deficiency).

questions.stem: The PINEAL gland in the brain secretes which hormone, regulating sleep-wake cycles?

options.option_text: Cortisol, the body's main stress hormone
Melatonin, peaking at night to induce sleep
Insulin, lowering blood glucose levels
Aldosterone, regulating electrolyte balance

questions.explanation: Pineal gland — small (pea-sized) endocrine gland in the brain. Secretes MELATONIN — peaks at night, low during day → entrains circadian rhythm. Used as supplement for jet lag, insomnia. Light exposure (especially blue light from screens) suppresses melatonin → modern sleep disruption. Descartes once called pineal 'the seat of the soul' (incorrect, but historically influential). Distractor 1 = adrenal cortex. Distractor 3 = pancreas beta cells. Distractor 4 = adrenal cortex.

questions.stem: THYROXINE (T4), secreted by the thyroid gland, contains which essential trace element?

options.option_text: Iron, like haemoglobin in red blood cells
Iodine, four atoms in each T4 molecule
Zinc, like several digestive enzymes
Selenium, like glutathione peroxidase enzymes

questions.explanation: THYROXINE (T4) — has 4 iodine atoms. Less active form. Converted to T3 (TRIIODOTHYRONINE, 3 iodine atoms) — biologically more active. Functions: regulate basal metabolic rate, body heat, growth, protein synthesis. IODINE deficiency → goitre, hypothyroidism, cretinism in children. India's Universal Salt Iodisation (USI) program addresses this. Distractor 1 = haemoglobin. Distractor 3 = zinc enzymes. Distractor 4 = selenium-dependent enzymes (Se does play role in thyroid hormone activation but not as the structural atom).
